newsitem.title: USA: Pioneer Oil files for bankruptcy protection.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer Oil files for bankruptcy protection.

text.p: Pioneer Oil and Gas said Friday it had sought protection under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code, citing pending litigation with Unocal Corp.
Pioneer said it filed for protection on Wednesday and it intends to deal with all creditors' claims, including those of Unocal, in the context of a Chapter 11 reorganization.
"Pioneer believes a plan of reorganization will be proposed as soon as possible and hopes to emerge from bankruptcy in a reasonable amount of time," it said.
The Salt Lake City-based company said that Unocal's claim against it "is the sole responsibility of (Mobil Corp unit) Mobil Oil Corporation."

A month ago, Pioneer said a jury had decided it must pay Unocal $563,158 arising from litigation involving an oilfield in the Santa Maria Valley in California. It said it planned to appeal the decision, which found that Pioneer was liable to Unocal for breach of contract, among other things.
In its statement today, Pioneer's president, Don Colton, noted that the original lawsuit filed in California named both Mobil and Pioneer as defendants.
He said Unocal, pressured by Mobil on other California projects, dropped Mobil from the lawsuit.

Pioneer failed in an attempt to bring Mobil back into the litigation and Pioneer has been forced to sue Mobil separately in Salt Lake City, he said. Pioneer accuses Mobil of fraud in selling it the Santa Maria property for $12,365 without disclosing the existence of buried oil sumps which would be costly to clean up.
Colton said Pioneer believes that it will prevail against Mobil in the lawsuit and that Mobil will be responsible for all costs asserted by Unocal, which includes a cleanup bill of about $2 million.
In addition, Mobil may have to pay Pioneer punitive damages, Colton said.
"Our problem is timing; because of the California court decision, Unocal can obtain a judgment against Pioneer before we can prevail against Mobil," he said.
